validation.notes: The script links the real packages/coding-agent/src/core/project-trust.ts, settings-manager.ts and resource-loader.ts through .prale-eval/subject.mjs with boundary fakes (fs paths, DefaultPackageManager, extension loader, chalk/proper-lockfile stub) and runs five scenarios with node:assert/strict. Repairs: (1) project-trust.ts resolveProjectTrusted now denies (returns false) when the ask policy needs a prompt but projectTrustContext.hasUI is false, so a headless reload with no stored decision is not treated as consent; (2) settings-manager.ts setProjectTrusted(false) clears the cached project scope (it previously self-assigned, retaining project settings) while keeping global settings; (3) resource-loader.ts reload applies the resolver's boolean (it previously forced setProjectTrusted(true)), so revocation discards project configuration and removes project extensions from the next resolved set while global and CLI extensions remain, and a reload without a resolver keeps the existing trust state. Cross-module assertions cover: headless ask/always/never, stored decisions, --approve override, extension project_trust decisions with remember, interactive selection/dismissal, setProjectTrusted(false) dropping project settings and re-trusting restoring them, and an approved -> revoked -> resolver-less reload sequence checking getExtensions() paths, getProjectSettings(), getTheme() and isProjectTrusted(). Mutation check performed: restoring each of the three files alone to its faulty baseline makes the script fail with an AssertionError (exit 1, no crash/import error); with the repair all scenarios print ok and the run exits 0. No optional dependency was unavailable; no real time, randomness or external service is used for correctness evidence. Test inputs were created under .prale-eval/tmp-revocation-* by fs.mkdtempSync and removed in a finally block.
